_comment: The bracket tree's vocabulary: the Arabic name of each grammatical term and the colour it is drawn in, plus how the treebank build reads its records. The code holds no Arabic of its own, so a term is reworded by editing this file alone.
_terms_comment: role = what a piece does · label = what a unit is. tone names the colour the diagram draws it in; the frontend owns the actual value.

mawsool_silah.detail: الصِّلَةُ لَا مَحَلَّ لَهَا مِنَ الْإِعْرَابِ

harf_atf.detail: غَيْرُ عَامِلٍ، لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ مِنَ الْإِعْرَابِ

harf_istinaf.detail: غَيْرُ عَامِلٍ، لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ مِنَ الْإِعْرَابِ

_treebank_comment: Reading the Quranic Treebank (NoorBayan, MIT) into the same tree shape. It names a relation in Arabic for each word and points at the word that governs it; these tables say how those names are drawn. A name that matches nothing here still draws, it just takes the default colour, because the name itself is the fact, not the colour.

treebank._noun_only_comment: Jobs only a noun's ending can do inside its own word: a word whose pronoun is its مضاف إليه is a noun, whatever the treebank calls it (أَيُّهُمْ is an اسم استفهام, tagged حرف استفهام), since no particle takes a مضاف إليه.
treebank._tone_comment: Matched as substrings, first hit wins, so مفعول به and مفعول مطلق share one entry.
treebank._constituent_comment: Only the three the treebank's own documentation names plainly are given a wording. SC, S and CS are left unnamed rather than guessed at.
treebank._wording_comment: The treebank writes its relation names without vowels; the rest of the app writes them fully vowelled. Same terms, so they are spelled the app's way here. A name that is not in this list is shown exactly as the treebank wrote it, its own wording beats no wording.
treebank._connector_comment: The treebank gives a glued و / ف as a token of its own with no relation at all, because it governs nothing. These are the parts of speech that means, and what each one is called. A part of speech not listed here keeps whatever the treebank said about it.
treebank._frame_comment: A relation the treebank writes as two words, خبر / اسم plus the word that governs it. The frame is spelled the app's way; the governing word is too when it is listed below, and is otherwise left exactly as the treebank wrote it and marked as such.
treebank._particle_comment: What a particle is, in the treebank's own name for its part of speech (pos_ar), spelled the app's way. A word whose every piece is named here is a particle, and the diagram calls it what it is: لَا is a حَرْفُ نَفْيٍ, not the job of the word it governs. The treebank often hangs the governed word off the particle (يَعْلَمُ off لَا) and writes the particle's meaning on that arrow (نفي); an arrow whose name is already inside the particle's own name (نفي in حرف نفي, استفهام in حرف استفهام) is read as the particle's meaning, never as the governed word's job. Arrows the particle's name does not say (مجرور under حرف جر, منادى under حرف نداء, اسم إن under حرف نصب) stay with the governed word. A value that is a key of `terms` is that term, so a particle the rules also name (إِنَّ is the treebank's حرف نصب) is spelled once.
treebank._unit_head_comment: What a word is, for a word that heads a unit. The unit carries the job (the clause بُعْثِرَ مَا … is the شَرْطٌ, إِذَا with its clause is the مَفْعُوْلٌ بِهِ), so the word's own column says what it is rather than repeating that job. Keyed by the treebank's pos_ar; each value is a key of `terms`. A noun heading a unit is not listed: its job (مُبْتَدَأٌ, مُضَافٌ) is its own, and it keeps it.
